objective: Review the wrapper-mediated Verilator-process-to-launcher bridge boundary definition and decide whether it may advance to a scoped non-executing bridge fixture implementation without claiming direct Verilator sidecar execution, broad native option support, runtime/ABI change, timing evidence, or arbitrary filelist support.

review_decision.reason: The definition chooses wrapper-mediated process launch as the narrowest bridge kind that can add real Verilator-facing process parse evidence before the existing launcher path, while keeping parser success, reviewed fixture metadata, explicit sidecar context, structured launcher argv, sidecar stages, compare evidence, and timing evidence as separate authorities.
review_decision.weakest_point: The accepted boundary is still a definition. It does not implement a bridge, start a launcher from a real Verilator-facing process, prove direct Verilator sidecar execution, prove broad native option support, change runtime or ABI behavior, measure timing, infer arbitrary filelists, allocate GPUs automatically, require raw full-state equality, or prove production throughput.

the selected bridge kind is wrapper_mediated_process_launch_bridge
in-process Verilator callbacks and runtime/ABI extensions remain deferred
generated-command handoff alone is rejected as insufficient because it would repeat the reviewed metadata path
the scoped target remains pulp_ita_mha with config/slice_launch_templates/pulp_ita_mha.json and shape 64x1

failure classes remain distinguishable before any future run
generated reports and artifacts remain noncanonical
